summary: Ray and Emma return from an early dinner and a stroll to the observation deck, where Ray kissed her under a meteor she claimed was good luck. Emma invites him into her family's quarters, saying it would make Amah more comfortable with him after an awkward previous meeting. Ray privately has little interest in Amah or Frederick, and asks to meet the children Emma tutors, whom Emma says Amah's selected tutors manage while she only offers moral support.
one_line: Ray accompanies Emma to her family's quarters, where she plans to introduce him to Amah and the children in her care.
key_facts: Ray and Emma had gone for an early dinner before strolling up to the obs deck.
Ray told Emma about his supposed job, and Ziggy was riding his ass over his screw-ups.
Ray kissed Emma beneath the tail of a passing meteor on the obs deck because she said it was good luck.
Ray suspects Emma made up the good-luck claim on the spot so she could stick her tongue in his mouth.
Emma invites Ray in for a while, saying it would make Amah feel more comfortable with him.
Emma says Ray's previous meeting with Amah was a little awkward.
Ray says his schedule has become a bit more flexible lately.
Ray has no interest in talking to Amah again and does not care about her or Frederick.
Ray says he would like to meet the children who occupy so much of Emma's time.
Emma says Amah designs the schedule for the children's education.
The tutors Amah selected to travel with them implement the children's education schedule.
Emma says she is not very good with children and is there for moral support.
Emma keys in her entry code at the door, stopping the kako-daemon's warble.
Ray had been wondering how to let go of Emma's hand without seeming to avoid holding it in front of Amah and Whiston domestics.
Ray says the romantic dilemma has not changed since Julie Gentry, twenty years earlier.
